commit.subject: fix(auth): let Vertex AI authenticate with Application Default Credentials (#9017)
commit.body_excerpt:
* fix(auth): let Vertex AI authenticate with Application Default Credentials

Vertex AI auth required an API key, so an ADC or service account setup
could not start. Supplying a placeholder to satisfy the check made it
worse: an explicitly passed key switches the Google SDK to Vertex
Express mode, which clears the project and location and rejects the
request with "API keys are not supported by this API".

Treat a configured GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT as sufficient credentials for
the vertex-ai auth type, in both the CLI pre-flight check and the core
model config validation, and leave the API key absent so the SDK
resolves ADC itself. The missing-credentials errors now mention the
keyless path instead of pointing only at envKey.

Fixes #9016

* fix(auth): select Vertex mode explicitly and keep de

    fix(auth): let Vertex AI authenticate with Application Default Credentials (#9017)
    
    * fix(auth): let Vertex AI authenticate with Application Default Credentials
    
    Vertex AI auth required an API key, so an ADC or service account setup
    could not start. Supplying a placeholder to satisfy the check made it
    worse: an explicitly passed key switches the Google SDK to Vertex
    Express mode, which clears the project and location and rejects the
    request with "API keys are not supported by this API".
    
    Treat a configured GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT as sufficient credentials for
    the vertex-ai auth type, in both the CLI pre-flight check and the core
    model config validation, and leave the API key absent so the SDK
    resolves ADC itself. The missing-credentials errors now mention the
    keyless path instead of pointing only at envKey.
    
    Fixes #9016
    
    * fix(auth): select Vertex mode explicitly and keep declared key vars authoritative
    
    Review follow-ups on the Vertex ADC change.
    
    Vertex mode no longer depends on the GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI side effect.
    Only the CLI pre-flight check writes that variable, and the startup call to it
    sits under the sandbox branch, so a plain interactive or ACP session built a
    client pointed at the Gemini API endpoint instead of Vertex. The flag is now
    derived from the auth type at construction, and left untouched for the other
    auth types so the SDK keeps its own environment fallback there.
    
    An entry that declares its own key variable no longer falls through to ADC when
    that variable is unset. It keeps failing on the declared variable, so a secret
    that failed to inject cannot silently authenticate as a different principal.
    The keyless hint is suppressed for those entries as well, since it would be
    advice that cannot work.
    
    The ACP pre-flight cell reports an indeterminate state for a keyless Vertex
    setup rather than a confirmed token: a configured project is routing
    configuration, not evidence that a credential resolves. All three gates now
    share one definition of a configured project, so whitespace is handled the same
    way everywhere, and the CLI missing-key message carries the same keyless hint as
    the core errors.
    
    Docs corrected on two counts: the environment-only row now says a keyless setup
    must select the auth type explicitly, since it is not inferred from the project
    alone, and the provider note names every key source the resolver folds in.
    
    ---------
    
    Co-authored-by: Shaojin Wen <shaojin.wensj@alibaba-inc.com>

episode.before: At parent c776c665b00a39d55c470beb788a2b9a77a2feb7, credential loading returned the first parseable object from the default cache path or GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS. episode.after: At f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297, credential sources are collected into an ordered list. The explicit cloud access-token override remains first; otherwise each cached candidate is verified sequentially using a credential-type-appropriate client. Verification failures are logged and resolution continues to the next candidate, allowing GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS to authenticate when a higher-priority cache entry is invalid. Successful default credentials still retain priority.
episode.diff: The change replaces a first-parseable-credential loader with an ordered candidate collector, adds tolerant encrypted-storage loading, generalizes non-authorized-user credential classification, factors consistent OAuth client construction and token-event handling, and changes initialization to verify candidates one at a time until one succeeds. It adds a regression test where an expired default refresh token is rejected and a valid GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS refresh token is subsequently selected. evidence_units.claim: Pinned commit f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297 has parent c776c665b00a39d55c470beb788a2b9a77a2feb7, is titled "fix(core): sequentially verify cached credentials and restore GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS fallback (#28472)", and modifies the OAuth implementation and its tests.

Before the change, fetchCachedCredentials returned immediately on the first parseable credential object; the ordered paths placed the default cache before GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, and encrypted storage was returned directly.

Before the change, initOauthClient verified only the single credential returned by fetchCachedCredentials; a caught verification failure then proceeded to later interactive or compute authentication logic rather than another file credential.

The replacement fetchCachedCredentialsList accumulates credentials in priority order, isolates load and parse failures per source, includes GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS after the default file when unencrypted storage is used, and returns all successfully parsed candidates.

initOauthClient now iterates through the ordered candidate list. Non-authorized-user typed credentials are adapted through GoogleAuth, while OAuth credentials are assigned to a newly configured OAuth2 client and checked with getAccessToken plus getTokenInfo. Errors are caught per candidate so the loop can continue.

A shared OAuth2-client factory preserves proxy configuration, token persistence, and post-authentication callbacks for the access-token override, every OAuth credential candidate, and later authentication flows.

The public getOauthClient entry point memoizes and invokes initOauthClient, so callers of the existing authentication API receive the revised ordered resolution behavior without an API signature change.

Existing credential-order tests establish that a valid default cache remains preferred, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS is used when the default is missing, and typed external credentials are adapted through GoogleAuth.

The added regression test creates an expired default refresh token and a valid environment-file refresh token, makes token verification reject the default, invokes getOauthClient, and asserts that the environment credential is eventually assigned.

The committed regression oracle verifies the repaired transition from invalid higher-priority credentials to valid lower-priority credentials while the neighboring tests guard the intended priority and credential-type behavior. No test execution result was available from the inspected evidence bundle.

title: Preserve explicitly configured credential-profile precedence over ambient access keys
before: At parent commit 04b15259b216294038169664aa4782d777b0281f, the Bedrock client selected a profile from the explicit profile option or provider/environment lookup, but independently converted available AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY values into config.credentials. When a profile supplied by the application's stored-auth flow coexisted with ambient access keys, both profile and explicit credentials were passed to the SDK, whose explicit credentials took precedence and caused the configured profile to be ignored.
after: At commit b63403a50f57fa0e3098684e927a63279598ec89, client construction first distinguishes an application-configured profile—options.profile or the provider-scoped options.env.AWS_PROFILE—from an ambient profile. It still passes the selected profile to the SDK, but only injects access-key credentials when no application-configured profile exists. Ambient access keys remain usable when no profile is configured and retain the prior behavior when the profile itself is only ambient.
diff: The implementation adds an optionsProfile value, uses it before ambient AWS_PROFILE lookup when setting config.profile, and changes the access-key assignment guard from `!skipAuth && credentials` to `!skipAuth && credentials && !optionsProfile`. A new mocked client-construction test suite checks explicit and provider-scoped profile precedence, the no-profile access-key fallback, and the intentionally unchanged ambient-profile-plus-access-keys case.

commit.subject: fix(ai): prefer configured Bedrock profile over ambient AWS keys (#7176)
commit.body_excerpt:
Bedrock profile configured via pi's auth flow was ignored when ambient
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY were set, because pi forced
config.credentials from those keys and the SDK treats explicit
credentials as overriding config.profile.

Fixes #6957

episode.title: Preserve explicitly configured credential-profile precedence over ambient access keys
episode.before: At parent commit 04b15259b216294038169664aa4782d777b0281f, the Bedrock client selected a profile from the explicit profile option or provider/environment lookup, but independently converted available AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY values into config.credentials. When a profile supplied by the application's stored-auth flow coexisted with ambient access keys, both profile and explicit credentials were passed to the SDK, whose explicit credentials took precedence and caused the configured profile to be ignored.
episode.after: At commit b63403a50f57fa0e3098684e927a63279598ec89, client construction first distinguishes an application-configured profile—options.profile or the provider-scoped options.env.AWS_PROFILE—from an ambient profile. It still passes the selected profile to the SDK, but only injects access-key credentials when no application-configured profile exists. Ambient access keys remain usable when no profile is configured and retain the prior behavior when the profile itself is only ambient.
episode.diff: The implementation adds an optionsProfile value, uses it before ambient AWS_PROFILE lookup when setting config.profile, and changes the access-key assignment guard from `!skipAuth && credentials` to `!skipAuth && credentials && !optionsProfile`. A new mocked client-construction test suite checks explicit and provider-scoped profile precedence, the no-profile access-key fallback, and the intentionally unchanged ambient-profile-plus-access-keys case.

evidence_units.claim: Commit b63403a50f57fa0e3098684e927a63279598ec89 identifies the defect: a profile configured through the application auth flow was ignored when ambient AWS access keys existed because explicit SDK credentials override config.profile.

The parent implementation assigned config.profile from `options.profile || getProviderEnvValue("AWS_PROFILE", options.env)` and later assigned resolved access-key credentials whenever authentication was not skipped, without guarding against an application-configured profile.
evidence_units.source: git diff 04b15259b216294038169664aa4782d777b0281f b63403a50f57fa0e3098684e927a63279598ec89 -- packages/ai/src/api/bedrock-converse-stream.ts; removed lines in the client-configuration hunk

evidence_units.claim: The changed implementation defines `optionsProfile` as `options.profile || options.env?.AWS_PROFILE`, uses it before ambient profile lookup, and suppresses explicit access-key injection when optionsProfile is present.
evidence_units.source: packages/ai/src/api/bedrock-converse-stream.ts at b63403a50f57fa0e3098684e927a63279598ec89; client-configuration hunk adding optionsProfile and `credentials && !optionsProfile`

evidence_units.claim: The runtime stream options support both a direct profile option and a provider-scoped environment map, which are the two application-controlled profile inputs recognized by the new precedence guard.
evidence_units.source: packages/ai/src/api/bedrock-converse-stream.ts at b63403a50f57fa0e3098684e927a63279598ec89; BedrockOptions.profile and stream use of options.env.AWS_PROFILE

evidence_units.claim: The new test supplies ambient access keys with an explicit profile and with a scoped AWS_PROFILE, then asserts that the constructed client config contains the selected profile and no explicit credentials.
evidence_units.source: packages/ai/test/bedrock-credentials.test.ts at b63403a50f57fa0e3098684e927a63279598ec89; test `prefers explicit and scoped profiles over ambient AWS access keys`

evidence_units.claim: The new test verifies that ambient access keys are still converted into explicit client credentials when no profile is configured.
evidence_units.source: packages/ai/test/bedrock-credentials.test.ts at b63403a50f57fa0e3098684e927a63279598ec89; test `uses ambient AWS access keys when no profile is configured`

evidence_units.claim: The new test documents that an ambient AWS_PROFILE alone does not suppress ambient access keys: both profile and explicit credentials remain in the client config.
evidence_units.source: packages/ai/test/bedrock-credentials.test.ts at b63403a50f57fa0e3098684e927a63279598ec89; test `uses ambient AWS access keys when only an ambient profile is set`

evidence_units.claim: The pinned commit changes one runtime implementation file and adds one 115-line credential-priority test file, with 123 insertions and 2 deletions overall.

The test harness mocks the SDK client, captures its constructor configuration, and asserts exactly one client construction, providing an isolated oracle for credential-resolution output without making a provider request.
evidence_units.source: packages/ai/test/bedrock-credentials.test.ts at b63403a50f57fa0e3098684e927a63279598ec89; mocked BedrockRuntimeClient and captureClientConfig helper

candidate_atomics.name: prefer_application_configured_profile
candidate_atomics.description: Recognize profile selections originating from explicit runtime configuration or provider-scoped stored configuration and prevent ambient access keys from overriding them through an explicit credentials field.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure an application-selected credential profile remains the effective authentication source when conflicting ambient access keys are present.
semantic_action.pre_state: A client request has an explicitly supplied or provider-scoped profile, while ambient access-key variables may also be available.
semantic_action.post_state: The client configuration carries the selected profile and omits explicit access-key credentials, allowing the SDK profile resolution path to remain authoritative.
semantic_action.validation: Capture the constructed SDK client configuration under explicit-profile-plus-ambient-keys and scoped-profile-plus-ambient-keys scenarios; assert the expected profile and an undefined credentials field.

candidate_atomics.name: preserve_ambient_access_key_fallback
candidate_atomics.description: Retain existing access-key behavior outside the narrowly defined application-configured-profile case, including the documented ambient-profile combination.

semantic_action.intent: Avoid disabling valid ambient access-key authentication while repairing configured-profile precedence.
semantic_action.pre_state: Ambient access keys are present and no profile is supplied through explicit or provider-scoped application configuration.
semantic_action.post_state: The client receives explicit access-key credentials; an ambient-only profile, if present, is not treated as an application ownership signal and remains alongside those credentials.
semantic_action.validation: Capture client configurations for ambient keys without a profile and for ambient keys with only an ambient profile; assert that the access-key pair remains present in both cases.

candidate_atomics.name: validate_credential_source_precedence_matrix
candidate_atomics.description: Exercise conflicting and fallback credential-source combinations at the SDK client-construction boundary.

semantic_action.intent: Prove both the repaired precedence rule and its non-regression boundaries.
semantic_action.pre_state: The client constructor can be intercepted and runtime environment values can be isolated per scenario.
semantic_action.post_state: Tests distinguish application-configured profiles from ambient profiles and verify the resulting profile and credentials fields for all covered combinations.
semantic_action.validation: Run the three mocked constructor scenarios and compare the emitted client configuration against the expected precedence matrix.

candidate_workflows.name: repair_configured_credential_source_precedence
candidate_workflows.description: Repair a provider adapter that translates ambient credentials into an explicit SDK field which unintentionally overrides a credential source deliberately selected through application configuration.

workflow_graph.goal: Make an application-configured credential profile authoritative over conflicting ambient access keys without removing ambient credential fallback behavior.
workflow_graph.entry_state: The adapter independently sets a selected profile and explicit credentials, so the downstream SDK's own precedence rules cause ambient keys to defeat the application's configured profile.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Application-configured profiles suppress explicit ambient-key injection, fallback access keys still work when no application-configured profile exists, and tests encode both the repaired and unchanged cases.
